nodes.statement: Let $f$ be the constant function 1, and let $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1(\R)$. Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{2\epsilon}\int_{-\e}^\e|g(x-t^2)|dt \simeq \sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{\e}\int_\e^{2\e} |g(x-t^2)|dt. \end{align*} Notice that for any $\e>0$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\e}\int_\e^{2\e}|g(x-t^2)|dt=\frac{1}{\e}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}\frac{|g(x-u)|}{2\sqrt{u}}du\ge \frac{1}{4\e^2}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}|g(x-u)|du. \end{align*} Then, for $x>2$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}} \int_{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}^{2\,\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}|g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{x+1} \int\limits_{(x+1)/4}^{4(x+1)/4} |g(x-u)|du \gtrsim \frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*} Therefore, $M(f,g) \not\in L^1(\R)$.
nodes.statement_short: Change variables $u=t^2$ to compare the average with $\frac{1}{4\e^2}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}|g(x-u)|du$, then choose $\e=\sqrt{(x+1)/4}$ to get $\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}$ for $x>2$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Fix the low-frequency indices and record the size of the phase
nodes.statement: Fix $m,n \in\Z_-$. From the definition of $\phi$ we have that $\big|\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\big|, \big|\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\big|\lesssim 1$, and by property (3) as part of the definition of $\NF$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness}, we have \[ \sup\limits_{t\in\supp\underline{\rho}}\Big|\eta\gamma\Big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}} \Big)\Big|<C_\gamma, \] where $C_\gamma$ is a positive constant that is allowed to change from line to line.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $m,n\in\Z_-$ and record the bounds on $\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}$, $\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}$ and $\eta\gamma(t2^{-j(x)})$ coming from property (3) of $\NF$.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion of the phase
nodes.statement: Recalling now \eqref{M_multiplierr} - \eqref{mjmn}, we develop the phase in \eqref{phmultiplier} in a Taylor series \begin{align} m_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta)&=\Bigg(\int_\R \sum_{k\in\N} \frac{(-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t)^k}{k!}\sum_{l\in\N}\frac{(i\eta\gamma(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}))^l}{l\,!}\underline{\rho}(t)dt\Bigg)\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}} \Big)\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big)\nonumber\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big), \end{align} where \[ C_{k,l}=C_{j(x),k,l}:=\int_\R t^k\Big(\frac{\gamma(2^{-j(x)}t)}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)^l \underline{\rho}(t)dt. \]
nodes.statement_short: Expand both exponentials in Taylor series, producing the coefficients $C_{k,l}$.

nodes.name: Absolute convergence of the Taylor series
nodes.statement: Since \begin{equation} |C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l} \end{equation} uniformly in $x$, the sum \eqref{taylor-series} converges absolutely.
nodes.statement_short: Since $|C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l}$ uniformly in $x$, the double series converges absolutely.

nodes.name: Introduce the low-frequency cut-off $\psi$
nodes.statement: Set now \begin{equation} \psi(x):=\sum_{m<0}\phi(\frac{x}{2^m})\,, \end{equation} and notice that $\psi\in\s(\R)$ since $\psi=1-\sum_{m\ge0}\phi_m.$
nodes.statement_short: Set $\psi=\sum_{m<0}\phi(\cdot/2^m)$ and note $\psi=1-\sum_{m\ge0}\phi_m\in\s(\R)$.

nodes.name: Insert the expansion into $m^L_{j(x)}$
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{taylor-series} in \eqref{low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation21}, we have \begin{align} m^L_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\psi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l \psi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big),\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \,\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Substituting the Taylor expansion into the low-frequency multiplier gives a series in $\tilde\psi_k$ and $\tilde\psi_l$.

nodes.name: Convolution form of $\M^L_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Thus, putting together \eqref{lowTaylor} and \eqref{operator_low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation22}, we have \begin{align} \M_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\int_\R \hat{f}(\xi)\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)e^{i\xi x}d\xi\Big) \Big(\int_\R \hat{g}(\eta)\tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) e^{i\eta x}d\eta\Big)\nonumber\\ &\approx\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k }{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x).\nonumber \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\M^L_\Gamma(f,g)$ as a series of products of convolutions of $f$ and $g$ against dilated derivatives of $\check\psi$.

nodes.name: Domination of each factor by the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function
nodes.statement: We can construct the function $\phi$ such that for every $k\in\N$, the function $\check{\psi}^{(k)}$ has an integrable radially decreasing majorant $\Phi_k$ with $\|\Phi_k\|_1\lesssim C^k$ for some constant $C>0$. Thus, using a classical result in \cite{stein1993harmonic}, one has \begin{align} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|&\le \sup_{t>0} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{t}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{t}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\nonumber\\ &\le \|\Phi_k\|_1 Mf(x)\nonumber\\ &\lesssim C^k Mf(x). \end{align} Analogously, \begin{equation} \Big|\Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\lesssim C^l Mg(x). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Using integrable radially decreasing majorants and a classical result of Stein, each factor is $\lesssim C^kMf(x)$ resp. $\lesssim C^lMg(x)$.

nodes.name: Summation of the series: the pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Putting together \eqref{low_frequency}, \eqref{Mf} and \eqref{Mg} we have \begin{align*} |\M_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|&\lesssim \sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}|C_{k,l}|C^{k+l}Mf(x)Mg(x)\\ &\lesssim Mf(x)Mg(x)\sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}C_\gamma^{k+l} C^{k+l}\\ &\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x),\numberthis \end{align*} where here we used \eqref{constcont}. Therefore, \eqref{pointwise_maximal} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Summing the absolutely convergent series yields $|\M^L_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x)$.

nodes.name: From the pointwise bound to the $L^r$ bound
nodes.statement: Taking now $p,\, q,\, r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}, H\"older’s inequality and the standard $L^p$ strong type estimate for the classical Hardy-Littlewood maximal function imply \begin{align*} \|\M_\Gamma^L(f,g)\|_r&\lesssim_\gamma\|Mf Mg\|_r\lesssim_{p,q} \|Mf\|_p\|Mg\|_q\lesssim_{p,q} \|f\|_p \|g\|_q, \end{align*} which concludes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality plus the $L^p$ strong-type estimate for $M$ give the $L^r$ bound.

nodes.name: Integration by parts: splitting the symbol
nodes.statement: Fix a pair $(m,n)\in\Z^2\setminus((\Z_-)^2\cup\Delta)$. As in the proof of \cite[Claim 1]{lie2015boundedness}, integrating by parts, we write \[ m_{j(x),m,n}=A_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta)+B_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta), \] where \begin{equation} A_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta):=\Big(\int_\R e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t} e^{i\eta\gamma(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}})} \frac{i\ \underline{\rho}'(t)}{-\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\frac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\gamma'\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}dt\Big) \phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}} \Big) \phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} B_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta):= \Big(\int\limits_\R e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t}e^{i\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)} \frac{-i\frac{\eta}{2^{2j(x)}}\gamma''\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)} {\Big({-\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\frac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\gamma'\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}\Big)^2} \underline{\rho}(t)dt\Big) \phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big)\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrating by parts writes $m_{j(x),m,n}=A_{j(x),m,n}+B_{j(x),m,n}$, with the derivative of the phase in the denominator.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Case 1: geometric expansion when $m-n\ge C_\gamma$
nodes.statement: \item \textsf{Case 1}: $m-n\ge C_\gamma>>1$ $\newline$ By (3) in the definition of $\NF$, we have that \[ \tfrac{1}{-\tfrac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\tfrac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\gamma'\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}=-\tfrac{1}{2^m}\frac{1}{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}} \sum_{l\in\N} \tfrac{1}{2^{l(m-n)}}\Bigg(\frac{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}}{\frac {\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}}\Bigg)^l (Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)}(t))^l. \]
nodes.statement_short: When $m-n\gg1$ the reciprocal of the phase derivative expands in a geometric series in $2^{-l(m-n)}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: The pieces $A_{j(x),m,n,l}$ and their well-behaved bumps
nodes.statement: \[ A_{j(x),m,n}=\sum_{l\in\N} A_{j(x),m,n,l}, \] with \begin{align*} A_{j(x),m,n,l}(\xi,\eta)&=-\frac{1}{2^m}\frac{1}{2^{l(m-n)}} \left(\int_\R e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t} e^{i\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)} i\,\underline{\rho}'(t) (Q'(t)+Q_{j(x)}(t))^l dt\right)\\ &\hspace{2.5cm}\times \tilde{\phi}_{-l-1}\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big)\tilde{\phi}_{l} \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big) \end{align*} where here $\tilde{\phi}_{l}$, $l\in\Z$, is smooth, compactly supported away from the origin, and obeying \[ \|\tilde{\phi}_{l}\|_{C^\beta}\lesssim\beta!\,(|l|+\b)^{\b}\, C^{|l|+\b} \] for $\b\in\N$ and some fixed $C>0$. We recall now the fact that, from the properties of $\g\in\NF$ one has that $\|Q_j\|_{C^N}\le a_j$ with $a_j\to 0$ as $j\to\infty$ and thus, since $|j(x)|\geq j_0$, one can choose $j_0\in\N$ large enough so that $\|Q_{j(x)}\|_{C^N}\leq \|Q\|_{C^N}\:\:\textrm{a.e.}\:x\in\R$.
nodes.statement_short: Split $A_{j(x),m,n}=\sum_l A_{j(x),m,n,l}$ with symbols built from bumps $\tilde\phi_l$ of controlled $C^\beta$ norms, and fix $j_0$ so that $\|Q_{j(x)}\|_{C^N}\le\|Q\|_{C^N}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Pointwise estimate for $\Lambda^A_{m,n,l}$
nodes.statement:
Defining the operator $\Lambda^A$ as \[ \Lambda^A_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x):=\int_\R\int_\R \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta) A_{j(x),m,n,l}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d \eta, \] we have  egin{align} |\Lambda^A_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|&=\Big| rac{1}{2^m} rac{1}{2^{l(m-n)}} \int_\R (f*\check{	ilde{\phi}}_{-l-1,m+j(x)}) ig(x- rac{2^mt}{2^{m+j(x)}} ig)\ &\hspace{.1cm}	imes  ig(g* ig\{	ilde{\phi}_l ig(	frac{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}{2^n}\,\cdot ig) ig\} \check{\phantom{1}} ig) ig(x+\gamma(2^{-j(x)}t) ig) \,\underline{ho}'(t)\,(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)}(t))^l\, dt\Big|
onumber\ &\lesssim  rac{1}{2^m}\Big( rac{2\|Q'\|_\infty}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l \int\limits_{\{t\in\R: rac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} \sup_{j\in\Z}\Big|(f*\check{	ilde{\phi}}_{-l-1,j}) ig(x- rac{2^mt}{2^j} ig)\Big| 
onumber\ &\hspace{.5cm}	imes \sup_{j\in\Z}\Big| ig(g* ig\{ rac{1}{	frac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}} \check{	ilde{\phi}}_l ( rac{\cdot}{	frac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}}) ig\} ig) (x+\gamma(2^{-j}t))\,\Big|\,dt
onumber\:. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The operator with symbol $A_{j(x),m,n,l}$ is dominated pointwise by shifted convolution suprema of $f$ and $g$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Two routes: shifted maximal or shifted square functions
nodes.statement: Once at this point one can proceed in two ways: \begin{itemize} \item the simplest route is to apply the estimate \begin{equation} |\Lambda^A_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|\lesssim \frac{1}{2^m}\Big(\frac{C_{\g}}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l \int\limits_{\{\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} M^{(2^m t)}f(x)\,M^{(2^n)}_{\g_t} g(x)\,dt\,. \end{equation} \item alternatively, one can appeal to a shifted square function argument, and write \begin{equation} |\Lambda^A_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|\lesssim \frac{1}{2^m}\Big(\frac{C_{\g}}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l \left(\int\limits_{\{\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} S_{2^mt}^{\tilde{\phi}_{-l-1}}f(x)\,S_{n,\g_t}^{\tilde{\phi}_l}g(x)\,dt\right)\,. \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The pointwise expression can be bounded either by products of shifted maximal functions or by products of shifted square functions.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Summation in $l$ and the bound for $\Lambda^A_{m,n}$
nodes.statement: Let $\Lambda^A_{m,n}:=\sum_{l\in\N} \Lambda^A_{m,n,l}$. Using now Fubini, H\"older, Lemma \ref{shifted_max_funct} and \eqref{mv} (or alternatively, Lemma \ref{shifted_square_funct} and \eqref{sv}), one deduces \begin{equation} \|\Lambda^A_{m,n}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\frac{1}{2^m}(m_++10)(n_{+}+10)\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q\:. \end{equation} Similarly, one gets the analogues of \eqref{A1} for the multiplier $B_{j,m,n}$, where in this latter case one uses that $\frac{1}{2^{2j}}\gamma''(2^{-j}t)=2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})(Q''(t)+Q_j''(t))\,.$ $\newline$
nodes.statement_short: Fubini, Hölder and the shifted function lemmas give $\|\Lambda^A_{m,n}\|\lesssim 2^{-m}(m_++10)(n_++10)\|f\|_p\|g\|_q$; the $B$ symbol is analogous.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Case 2: expansion when $n-m>C_\g$
nodes.statement: \item \textsf{Case 2}: $n-m>C_\g>>1$ $\newline$ As we did in Case 1, we write \[ \frac{1}{-\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\frac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}} \gamma'(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}})} =\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}} \sum_{l\in\N}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \Bigg(\frac{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}} {\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}}\Bigg)^l\frac{1}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)} (t))^{l+1}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: When $n-m\gg1$ the reciprocal is expanded with the roles of $\xi$ and $\eta$ exchanged.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: The pieces $\tilde A_{j(x),m,n,l}$ and the $2^{-n}$ bound
nodes.statement: Write \[ \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n}=\sum_{l\in\N}\tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}, \] where \begin{align*} \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}(\xi,\eta)&=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \left(\int_\R e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t}e^{i\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}i \frac{\underline{\rho}'(t)}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)}(t))^{l+1}}dt\right) \\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \tilde{\phi}_{l}\left(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\right)\,\tilde{\phi}_{-l-1}\left(\frac{ \gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\,\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\right). \end{align*} Letting $\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}$ be the operator with symbol $\tilde{A}_{j(\cdot),m,n,l}$ one proceeds as before in order to get \begin{equation*} |\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|\lesssim \frac{1}{2^n}\,\Big(\frac{C_{\g}}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l\,\left(\int\limits_{\{\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} M^{(2^m t)}f(x)\,M^{(2^n)}_{\g_t} g(x)\,dt\right) \,, \end{equation*} and respectively \begin{equation} \|\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \frac{1}{2^n}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\, \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{q}. \end{equation} Again, a similar reasoning applies to the multiplier $\tilde{B}_{j(\cdot),m,n}$.
nodes.statement_short: The same reasoning applied to $\tilde A_{j(x),m,n,l}$ yields the bound with $2^{-n}$ in place of $2^{-m}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Summation over $(m,n)$
nodes.statement: Putting together all of the above, one concludes \begin{align*} \|M_\Gamma^{H\not\Delta}(f,g)\|_r &\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \sum_{\substack{(m,n)\in \Z^2\setminus((\Z_-)^2\cup\Delta)\\ m-n\geq C_{\g}}} \frac{1}{2^m}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q\\ &\hspace{1cm} + \sum_{\substack{(m,n)\in \Z^2\setminus((\Z_-)^2\cup\Delta)\\ n-m\geq C_{\g}}} \frac{1}{2^n}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q\\ &\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Summing the geometric factors over both off-diagonal regions concludes the global estimate.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Littlewood-Paley form of the fixed-$j$ decay bound
nodes.statement: Using the following standard notation $\phi_{m+j}(\xi):=\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}\Big)$ and $\phi_{\gamma,m,j}(\eta):= \phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}\Big)$ we rewrite \eqref{l2c} in Theorem \ref{smallk2} as \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2\,\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the key $2^{-\epsilon m}$ bound with the frequency-localized pieces $f*\check\phi_{m+j}$ and $g*\check\phi_{\gamma,m,j}$.

nodes.name: Summation in $j$
nodes.statement: Using this together with \eqref{Tm} we deduce that $$\|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\leq \sum_{j\in\Z}\|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2\,\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}$$
nodes.statement_short: By the definition of $T_m$, sum the fixed-$j$ bounds over $j\in\Z$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz in $j$
nodes.statement: which, via an application of Cauchy-Schwarz, further gives $$\lesssim 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\left(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2^2\right)^\frac{1}{2}\, \left(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}^2\right)^\frac{1}{2} \lesssim 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_2\,,$$
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz splits the $j$-sum into two $\ell^2$ square sums.

nodes.name: Almost disjointness of the frequency supports
nodes.statement: where in the last inequality we used that the supports of the functions $\{\phi_{m+j}\}_{\{j\in\Z\}}$ and respectively $\{\phi_{\gamma,m,j}\}_{\{j\in\Z\}}$ are almost disjoint, with the latter being a direct consequence of the properties of the curve $\gamma$ (see the property ``smoothness, no critical points, variation near $0$ and $\infty$" in the definition of $\NF$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness}).
nodes.statement_short: The supports of $\{\phi_{m+j}\}_j$ and $\{\phi_{\gamma,m,j}\}_j$ are almost disjoint by the properties of $\gamma$, which concludes the bound.

nodes.name: Introduce the sublinear form $\Lambda_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Fix $p,\,p'$ as in our hypothesis and take $f\in L^p$ and $g\in L^{p'}$. In the spirit of \cite[Section 3]{lie2015triangle}, for $h\in L^{\infty}$ (we will assume from now on wlog that $\|h\|_{\infty}=1$ and $h$ is positive), we define\footnote{It is important to notice here that as opposed to the similar object defined in \cite{lie2015triangle}, in our context, in definition \eqref{Ljm} below, the operator $T_{j,m}(f,g)$ is taken with \emph{absolute values} thus making $\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)$ a sublinear ``form".} for each $j\in\Z$ and $m\in\N$ \begin{equation} \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h):=\int_\R |T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)|\, h(x)\,dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fix $p,p'$ and pair $|T_{j,m}(f,g)|$ against a positive $h\in L^\infty$ with $\|h\|_\infty=1$.

nodes.name: Split into $\Lambda_m^+$ and $\Lambda_m^-$
nodes.statement: For $m\in\N$, we define \begin{equation} \Lambda_m(f,g,h):=\Lambda_m^+(f,g,h)+\Lambda_m^-(f,g,h), \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \Lambda_m^+(f,g,h):=\sum_{j\in\N} \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)\quad \text{ and } \quad \Lambda_m^-(f,g,h):=\sum_{j\in\Z\setminus\N} \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Separate the positive and non-positive scales $j$.

nodes.name: Linearization of the absolute values
nodes.statement: Since our $\Lambda's$ involve absolute values inside the integral expressions, in order to be able to use the techniques in \cite{lie2015triangle}, we will first apply a linearization procedure. Thus, for a suitable sequence of $L^{\infty}-$functions $\{\ep_{j,m}\}$ with the property $|\ep_{j,m}(x)|=1$ a.e $x\in\R$, we will re-write \begin{equation} \Lambda_m^+(f,g,h):=\sum_{j\in\N} \int_{\R} T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)\, \ep_{j,m}(x)\,h(x)\,dx,\, \end{equation} with the obvious correspondence for $\Lambda_m^-(f,g,h)$.
nodes.statement_short: Unimodular multipliers $\ep_{j,m}$ turn the sublinear forms into linear ones.

nodes.name: Reduction to the estimate for $\Lambda^{\pm}_m$
nodes.statement: Deduce now that \eqref{l2cpp} is in fact equivalent with \begin{equation} \left|\Lambda_m^{\pm}(f,g,h)\right|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{p'}\,\|h\|_{\infty}. \end{equation} In what follows we will only focus on the $+$ component since the $-$ component can be treated in a similar fashion.
nodes.statement_short: The tame bound is equivalent to $|\Lambda_m^{\pm}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m\|f\|_p\|g\|_{p'}\|h\|_\infty$; only the $+$ part is treated.

nodes.name: Case $1<p\le2$: Littlewood-Paley and Fefferman-Stein
nodes.statement: \noindent\textbf{Case 1.} $1<p\leq 2$ $\newline$ With the notations\footnote{We will only recall here that $\phi_{j,p_0}(\eta):= \phi(\frac{\g'(2^{-j})\,\eta}{2^j}-p_0) $ and $\psi_{m,p_0,j}(\xi):= 2^{-\frac{m}{2}}\,e^{- i p_0 R(\frac{\xi}{2^j\,p_0})}\,\phi(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}})$ where $j\in\N$ and $p_0\in [2^m,\, 2^{m+1})\cap \N$ with $m\in\N$.} in \cite{lie2015triangle}, following the first part of the argument provided for the proof of Proposition 4.2 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}, we have $$|\ll_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\lesssim$$ $$\int_{\R}\left( \sum_{j\in\N}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(y)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\: \left( \sum_{j\in\N} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\ep_{j,m} h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)(y)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dy$$ $$\lesssim \left\| \left( \sum_{j\in\N}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\, \left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\N} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim \|f\|_{p}\,\left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\N}\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:,$$ where for the last relation we used standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for providing bounds on the square function for $f$) and Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the term involving the functions $g$ and $h$).
nodes.statement_short: Following the Banach-case argument, bound the form by a product of a square function in $f$ and a Fefferman-Stein maximal square function in $g,h$.

nodes.name: The $L^\infty$ contribution of $h$
nodes.statement: Using now that \begin{equation} ((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)=\int_{\R} (\ep_{j,m}\, h)(x-\frac{\g'(2^{-j})}{2^j}\,y)\,\check{\phi}(y)\,e^{i\,p_0\,y}\,dy\:, \end{equation} we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^2\lesssim_{\g} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A convolution identity shows the $p_0$-sum of $|(\ep_{j,m}h)*\check\phi_{j,p_0}|^2$ is $\lesssim_\g\|h\|^2_\infty$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz separating $g$ from $h$
nodes.statement: Thus, applying Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we get \begin{equation} \left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)^2\lesssim_{\g} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\,\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^2\,, \end{equation} from which we deduce that \begin{equation} |\ll_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\g} \|f\|_{p}\, \|h\|_{\infty}\,\left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\N}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz leaves only the double square function of $g$ times $\|h\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Rubio de Francia's inequality concludes Case 1
nodes.statement: Finally, since $p'\geq2$, we are allowed to apply Rubio de Francia's inequality (\cite{rubio1985littlewood}): \begin{equation} \left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\N}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\lesssim_{\g,p'} \|g\|_{p'}\:. \end{equation} Putting now together \eqref{CS}, \eqref{L}, \eqref{RF} we conclude that \eqref{l2cppg} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Since $p'\ge2$, Rubio de Francia's inequality bounds the double square function by $\|g\|_{p'}$.

nodes.name: Case $2<p<\infty$: Cauchy-Schwarz and Hölder
nodes.statement: \noindent\textbf{Case 2.} $2<p<\infty$ $\newline$ In this second case, we follow part of the argument inside the proof of Proposition 4.3 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}. Indeed, by applying Cauchy-Schwarz and then H\"older's inequality, we have \beq \eeq $$|\ll_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq$$ $$\sum_{j\in\N}\int_{\R} \,\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})(x)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\times \left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx$$ $$\leq\left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\N}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p} \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\N}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:.$$
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz in $p_0$ then Hölder splits the form into two double square functions.

nodes.name: Invoke the imported Proposition 4.4 and Lemma 4.9
nodes.statement: Now the content of Proposition 4.4 in \cite{lie2015triangle} is the statement that for $p\geq2$ one has \begin{equation} \left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\N}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\lesssim_{\g,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\;, \end{equation} while from the Lemma 4.9 in \cite{lie2015triangle} we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\ep_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\lesssim_{\g} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\, M(g*\check{\phi}_{\g,m,j})^2(x)\:, \end{equation} where here we recall that $\phi_{\g,m,j}(\eta):=\phi(\frac{\g'(2^{-j})}{2^{j+m}}\,\eta)\;.$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 4.4 controls the $f$-factor with the loss $m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}$ and Lemma 4.9 replaces the $g,h$-factor by $\|h\|_\infty M(g*\check\phi_{\g,m,j})$.

nodes.name: Conclusion of Case 2
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{Cf} and \eqref{claim} in \eqref{key2}, we conclude that \beq \eeq $$|\ll_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq_{\g,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\N} M(g*\check{\phi}_{\g,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim_{p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\N} (g*\check{\phi}_{\g,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\lesssim_{\g,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|g\|_{p'}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\,,$$ where we made use again of the Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the second inequality) and standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for the third inequality).
nodes.statement_short: Fefferman-Stein and Littlewood-Paley theory finish the tame bound.

nodes.name: Dualization: choice of $h\in L^{r'}$
nodes.statement: Using the notation from (\ref{Ljm}) and \cite{lie2015triangle}, we choose $h\in L^{r'}$ such that \[ \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)= \int_\R T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)h(x)dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: Pick $h$ realizing the $L^r$ norm so that $\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)=\int T_{j,m}(f,g)h$.

nodes.name: The two estimates for $|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|$
nodes.statement: Therefore \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\R |(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(x)\:|M\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot) (h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot)|\Bigg)(x)\,dx, \] and \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\R\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)(h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2} \Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m, p_0, j})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2}dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: Record the maximal-function form and the double square function form of the bound for $\Lambda_{j,m}$.

nodes.name: Transfer of the Banach-case results to $\Lambda_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Hence, by following the second part of the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.2 ]{lie2015triangle} and \cite[Proposition 4.3 ]{lie2015triangle}, we deduce that the results in \cite{lie2015triangle} hold for $\Lambda_{j,m}$. In particular, the analogue of \cite[Theorem 3.3]{lie2015triangle} follows:
nodes.statement_short: Following Propositions 4.2 and 4.3 of the Banach-case paper, its results hold for $\Lambda_{j,m}$, giving the edge estimates.

nodes.name: Real interpolation
nodes.statement: Thus, Proposition \ref{Tjmb} follows from the Proposition \ref{DeltaM} after applying real interpolation.
nodes.statement_short: Real interpolation between the edge $(AC)$ and edge $(AB)$ estimates gives the proposition.

nodes.name: Rewrite the fixed-$j$ bound for $p=q=2r$
nodes.statement: As we did for the proof of \eqref{l2c2}, we write \eqref{Tjm-pqr} as \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma}(1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}, \end{equation} where here we used that $p=q=2r$ and that $(2r)^*=\frac{2r}{2r-1}$ since $r\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Using $p=q=2r$ and $(2r)^*=\frac{2r}{2r-1}$, restate the bound with Littlewood-Paley pieces.

nodes.name: $\ell^r$ domination of the linearized operator and Hölder
nodes.statement: Since \begin{equation*} |T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)|\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}|T_{j,m}(f,g)|^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}, \end{equation*} it follows from H\"older inequality and Proposition \ref{Tjmb} that \begin{align} \big\|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\big\|_{L^r(dx)}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}\nonumber\\ &\le (1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}} \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Since $|T_{j(x),m}|\le(\sum_j|T_{j,m}|^r)^{1/r}$, Hölder and the fixed-$j$ bound give a $j$-sum of products.

nodes.name: Auxiliary $\ell^{2r}$ Littlewood-Paley estimate
nodes.statement: Notice that for $r\in [1,\infty)$ and for any $f, \phi\in\s(\R)$, we have \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\phi_j\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r}&\le \Bigg(\int_\R \sum_{j\in\Z}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^{2r}dx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r}\\ &\le \Bigg(\int_\R \Bigg(\sum_{j\in\Z}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^2\Bigg)^rdx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r} = \Bigg(\int_\R \Bigg\{\bigg(\sum_{j\in\Z}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^2\bigg)^\frac{1}{2}\Bigg\}^{2r}dx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r}\\ &=\Bigg\|\bigg(\sum_{j\in\Z}|f*\phi_j(x)|^2\bigg)^\frac{1}{2}\Bigg\|_{2r} \lesssim \|f\|_{2r}, \end{align*} here for the last relation we used standard Littlewood-Paley theory.
nodes.statement_short: For $r\in[1,\infty)$ one has $(\sum_j\|f*\phi_j\|_{2r}^{2r})^{1/2r}\lesssim\|f\|_{2r}$ by Littlewood-Paley theory.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz separating $f$ and $g$
nodes.statement: By Cauchy Schwartz, the hypothesis on $\g\in \NF$ and the result above, we obtain \begin{align} \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r}\Big(\sum_{j\in\Z}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r} \nonumber\\ &\le_{\g,r} \|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz plus the $\NF$ hypothesis bound the $j$-sum by $\|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}$.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{fg2r} in \eqref{supTjm} we get \begin{equation} \big\|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\big\|_{L^r(dx)}\le_{\g,r} (1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}, \end{equation} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Inserting the estimate gives the claimed $(1+m^{1-1/r})2^{-m/20r}$ bound.

nodes.name: Pointwise domination by $\|g\|_\infty Mf$
nodes.statement: From the definition \eqref{definition} of $M_\Gamma$ it is trivial to notice that for all $x\in\R$, \begin{align} |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|g\|_\infty\, \sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{2\e}\int_{-\e}^\e |f(x-t)|dt\nonumber\\ &\le \|g\|_\infty\, Mf(x). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bounding $|g|$ by $\|g\|_\infty$ leaves the symmetric average of $|f|$, which is $\le Mf(x)$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$

nodes.name: Apply the classical maximal function theory
nodes.statement: Hence, applying the classical results on the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator we get
nodes.statement_short: The $L^p$ boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator finishes the proof.
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$

nodes.name: Pointwise domination by $\|f\|_\infty M_\gamma g$
nodes.statement: From \eqref{discretizationc}, recalling that $\gamma\in\NF$ and our choice of $j_0$ in \eqref{threshold} - \eqref{threshold1}, we notice that for all $x\in\R$, \begin{align} |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|f\|_\infty\,M_\gamma\, g(x). \end{align} where here \begin{equation} M_\gamma\, g(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\Z}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bounding $|f|$ by $\|f\|_\infty$ leaves the curved average of $|g|$, i.e. the operator $M_\gamma g$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Reduction to the boundedness of $M_\gamma$
nodes.statement: Thus, Theorem \ref{finfty} follows from the result below
nodes.statement_short: Reduces to the $L^q$ bound for $M_\gamma$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Comparability of $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ on dyadic blocks
nodes.statement: From the properties of $\g$ and the choice of $j_0$ in \eqref{threshold} - \eqref{threshold1}, it is straightforward to check that for any $k\in \Z$ with $|k|>j_0$ and $t\in[2^k,2^{k+1}]$ one has \begin{equation} |\gamma(2^{k})|\approx_{\gamma} 2^{k}|\gamma'(t)|\approx_{\gamma}|\gamma(2^{k+1})|\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $|k|>j_0$ and $t\in[2^k,2^{k+1}]$ one has $|\gamma(2^k)|\approx_\gamma 2^k|\gamma'(t)|\approx_\gamma|\gamma(2^{k+1})|$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Change of variables $u=\gamma(t)$ on each block
nodes.statement: From \eqref{threshold1}, we deduce that $\gamma$ is strictly monotone and invertible over each of the intervals $(-\infty,-2^{j_0})$, $(-2^{-j_0},0)$, $(0,2^{-j_0})$ and $(2^{j_0}, \infty)$. Wlog we consider from now on that our entire discussion takes place relative to $J_0:=(2^{j_0}, \infty)$ and that both $\g'$ and $\g''$ are strictly positive on $J_0$. Thus, for $k\in\Z$ with $k>j_0$, one has \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt &=\frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{\gamma([2^k,2^{k+1}])}|g(x+u)|\frac{du}{|\gamma'(\gamma^{-1}(u))|}\\ &\le\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{\gamma(2^k)}^{\gamma(2^{k+1})}|g(x+u)|du\,. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Strict monotonicity and invertibility of $\gamma$ on the four intervals allow the substitution $u=\gamma(t)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Domination of each block average by $Mg$
nodes.statement: Appealing now to \eqref{gammak1t}, we deduce \begin{equation} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt \leq\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{-|\gamma(2^k)|-|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}^{|\gamma(2^k)|+|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}|g(x-u)|du \lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The comparability turns the block average into a symmetric average of $|g|$, hence $\lesssim_\gamma Mg(x)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: The negative block
nodes.statement: Analogously, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{-2^{k+1}}^{-2^k}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt&\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The blocks $[-2^{k+1},-2^k]$ are handled analogously.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Conclusion via the Hardy-Littlewood theory
nodes.statement: Therefore \begin{equation} \sup_{{j\in\Z}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\,\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation} Using now the standard theory on Hardy Littlewood maximal operator we conclude our Theorem \ref{Mgamma}.
nodes.statement_short: Taking the supremum in $j$ gives $M_\gamma g\lesssim_\gamma Mg$, and the classical theory concludes.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Choice of the counterexample
nodes.statement: Let $f=\chi_{[-1,1]}$ and $g=\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$ be characteristic functions, and let $\gamma(t)=t^2\in\NF$. Note that $f\in L^1(\R)$, $g\in L^\infty(\R)$ with $\|f\|_1=2$, and $\|g\|_\infty=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $f=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1$, $g=\chi_{(-\infty,1)}\in L^\infty$ and $\gamma(t)=t^2\in\NF$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Lower bound by the choice $\e=|x|+1$
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{2\e}\int\limits_{-\e}^\e |f(x-t)g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{2(|x|+1)}\int\limits_{-(|x|+1)}^{|x|+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Restricting the supremum to $\e=|x|+1$ gives a lower bound for $M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Evaluation for $x>2$
nodes.statement: Suppose $x>2$, then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\ge \frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt=\frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}g(x-t^2)dt\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For $x>2$ the integral is comparable to $1$, so $M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore, $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not absolutely integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not absolutely integrable.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Choice of the counterexample and reduction to annuli
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be the constant function 1, and let $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1(\R)$. Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{2\epsilon}\int_{-\e}^\e|g(x-t^2)|dt \simeq \sup_{\e>0}\frac{1}{\e}\int_\e^{2\e} |g(x-t^2)|dt. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take $f\equiv1$ and $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1$, and replace the symmetric average by an average over $[\e,2\e]$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Change of variables $u=t^2$
nodes.statement: Notice that for any $\e>0$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\e}\int_\e^{2\e}|g(x-t^2)|dt=\frac{1}{\e}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}\frac{|g(x-u)|}{2\sqrt{u}}du\ge \frac{1}{4\e^2}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}|g(x-u)|du. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Substituting $u=t^2$ bounds the average below by $\frac{1}{4\e^2}\int_{\e^2}^{4\e^2}|g(x-u)|du$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Choice $\e=\sqrt{(x+1)/4}$ for $x>2$
nodes.statement: Then, for $x>2$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}} \int_{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}^{2\,\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}|g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{x+1} \int\limits_{(x+1)/4}^{4(x+1)/4} |g(x-u)|du \gtrsim \frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: This choice makes the integral comparable to $1$, giving $\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore, $M(f,g) \not\in L^1(\R)$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $M(f,g)\notin L^1(\R)$.
